newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy coastguards trade fire with ship off Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy coastguards trade fire with ship off Albania.

text.p: An Italian coastguard patrol boat on Wednesday exchanged small arms fire off the northern Albanian coast with a boat carrying several hundred people, the defence ministry in Rome said in a statement.
The nationality of the boat was unknown but it was believed to have come from Yugoslav waters.

"An Italian coastguard patrol boat, which approached a vessel whose nationality was unknown off the northern Albanian coast and with several hundred people on board, was targeted by firearms from the boat itself," the ministry said.
"Our ship replied without victims or damage to either side," the statement added.
The ministry said the boat, about 30 metres (100 feet) long, was intercepted by the Italian navy and coastguard and was being guided to the Albanian port of Durres.

It said the incident showed that the navy's active patrolling of the Adriatic Sea between Italy and Albania under an accord between the two countries was "giving positive results in terms of tackling illegal immigration".
The ministry added however that there were signs that illegal immigration from Albania was being carried out now from points outside the troubled Balkan country.
More than 15,000 Albanians have crossed the Adriatic to Italy since a wave of violence swept the Balkan country in March after the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes.
Italy has sent thousands back, classing many as "undesirables", and has ships patrolling the Adriatic to intercept immigrants before they enter Italian waters.
Italy says the trafficking has become a lucrative business for organised criminal gangs.
